title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 196 (Appointment of managing director, whole-time director or manager)

content.overview: Section 196 regulates appointment and term of a managing director, whole-time director or manager, including the age band and the bar on simultaneous appointment of a manager and a managing director.
content.glance: Section 196 regulates appointment and term of a managing director, whole-time director or manager, including the age band and the bar on simultaneous appointment of a manager and a managing director.
content.study: Appointment is by the board and approved by members at the next general meeting. The term cannot exceed five years at a time, with reappointment permitted not earlier than one year before expiry. No person below twenty-one or who has attained seventy can be appointed, unless the seventy-year bar is relaxed by special resolution with an explanatory statement. A person cannot be both manager and managing director, or managing director of more than one company, except as the section allows for a second company with unanimous board consent and specific notice. Schedule V conditions and Central Government approval apply where the appointment does not meet the stated norms. Remuneration limits are in s. 197, not s. 196.

questionsAndAnswers.answer: Not always. It is required where the appointment does not satisfy the Schedule V conditions.

caseLaw.citation: Statutory appointment of managing director and manager
caseLaw.point: A managing director, whole-time director or manager is appointed for not more than five years, by the board and by a resolution at the next general meeting. The age and the no-conviction conditions in the section apply. This is a statutory pointer, not a judgment.
